title: Exclusive interview with Assistant GM Kyle Smith ahead of the 2026 NFL Draft | Miami Dolphins
text: What's up, Dolph fans? We are here with the team that's building the team in the 2026 NFL draft. Miami Dolphins, 11 picks this year. Cannot wait for it all and I cannot wait to talk to my next guest here, Kyle Smith, the assistant GM of your Miami Dolphins. Kyle, how you doing, man? >> Good, good. Appreciate you. >> Very happy to have you on here. Just first, how's it going getting your bearings in South Florida? How's your transition going to the new job here in Miami? >> It's been good. It's been really smooth. I'm still in a hotel, be locked up in a hotel for uh until after the draft. But um it's it really in short order since coming in here, you can find out right away that this is a first class organization. You know, all the way across the board, football operations, equipment staff, field staff, food, the food's been outstanding. Um you know, everyone talks about one of the first things they talk about when they get in here and and and I believe it. But uh it's been it's been great. >> Just wait till night one of the draft the spread they get out there. Yeah, I can't wait every morning for uh for breakfast, man. That's the best meal in my opinion. No doubt they they knock it out. The eggs benedict and the and the French toast today was >> whatever they put out there today. >> It was off the charts. So, take us more into kind of that process because obviously you're kind of getting your feet wet and getting your bearings here, but also the job is so wide ranging for an assistant GM. Can you just kind of take us through what some of your main duties are here at the Dolphins? Yeah, I'd say the, you know, obviously it's both sides, pro and college, you know, scouting and kind of overseeing both departments, but the main job for me is to create clarity, you know, for John Eric and and and halfway in the decision makers. Um, you know, obviously right now we're we're, you know, right in the midst of the draft preparation. Um, but even before that it was, you know, free agency and it's going through thorough, you know, process and meetings and, uh, grinding through everything and and we've got a really good staff and, uh, scouts, both pro and college. So, uh, that's really the main job is obviously the evaluations, overseeing both departments and doing everything you can to to create clarity for decision makers. >> Yeah, it makes perfect sense. Can you take us kind of into the the relationship with John Eric and yourself because obviously he's spoken very highly of you. I'm sure you've he's talked about you being a future GM in this league. Just uh how how has that relationship developed from where it was when it first started and to where it is now? >> Yeah, it's we go back a long ways. We kind of, you know, he's been in it a little bit longer than I have, you know, but we kind of cut our teeth together on the road as area scouts. And the way that it works is as scouts. He obviously was with the Packers. I was with, you know, Washington um at first. And you work with other scouts more than you work with your own scouts because you're out on the road with them. And so we developed a relationship back then. We went to from Southwest to Southeast, kept in contact. You always kind of surround yourself with guys that kind of think the same, work the same. We've always shared the same vision. We've always talked about these moments. If one were to get a GM job and the other one's coming with you, um, and and it just so happened to line up for us. So, um, he's a tremendous person. Uh, you know, obviously a really good scout and and an evaluator and, uh, couldn't be happier to be here with him. I imagine some of that time on the road provides a lot of value for what the job is now, right? In terms of delegating and working with the staff under you. >> Yeah, I think I think being, you know, anytime you're in personnel, it's, you know, the guys that are working for you, with you, you know, when you've been there and done that and and you're never going to ask guys to do something that you haven't done. And and that's a big emphasis from from J and myself. It's, you know, we're never going to ask guys to do stuff that that we haven't done at any point. And and, you know, I think that's a big part of it. That's a great managerial tool to have right there for sure. And being in the ind industry for so long, I'm sure you've learned a lot of different things about aspects of the job. What are some of the key things you picked up along the way that you hope to bring here to the Dolphins? >> Yeah, you know, there's there's so many I think sometimes it's it's we try to keep things simple, you know, and and it's take good football players. I know that sounds like obvious statement, but it is. There's a lot of different information that goes into we're a best player available team and that's how that's how we'll operate. I know John Eric has talked about that, but you know, there's so much information that goes into either signing a player in free agency or picking a player in the draft. You have all different avenues and and and data and information and the scouts opinions and and coaches opinions and everything. When it boils down to it, you're looking for that alignment um that everybody in the building sees it the same. Your convictions, do they have the character traits that we look for and do the is the skill set match what we look for? and and you pick the best player that's that's staring at you on the board. >> You talk about that shared aesthetic, right, in terms of getting guys on the same page. How do you go about developing that as a staff? Like obviously you and John Eric have a big hand in that, but how do you kind of get everyone aligned in terms of this is what we want it to look like and we need to all see it kind of similarly. >> Yeah, you try to have a you know everybody you want everyone's individual opinions. You don't want group you want group think to a point to have the shared vision u but you want individual opinions on the player. You don't want everybody to see it the same. Um, but when you bring, you know, the coaches in, when you bring scouts in, everybody who's who's talking about the individual player, um, they're the most important person in the room at that point. Um, and you take everybody's information that they have and you try to do the best you can to to collectively come together with that that shared vision. >> Yeah, it makes a lot of sense. And, you know, part of that is is building the draft board, right? That's one of those things where I'm sure it starts with a massive collection of names back in in in the summer and August and now you kind of whittle it down and and one of the questions I was most excited for anybody in this entire process was the lore behind building that draft board. I was hoping you can give us a bit of a look behind the scenes in terms of how that comes together from where it was back in August to where it comes now here coming up with the draft. >> Yeah, I mean it's it's obviously it's very long process, thorough process, but this is when it it really gets fun, you know, is this time of year. But, you know, it really starts in the summer before we show up at training camp. you know, in terms of the draft, you know, the the area scouts are the first boots on the ground. They put grades on guys and they go through the fall visits and then we have our February meetings. February meetings, it's really their time. The area scouts, the cross checkers to set that board, give their opinion, you know, the profile of the player. They've talked to everybody at every school call about the guy. Um, and then obviously as the baton kind of gets passed and then we got all-star games and then we get the combine and then here come the coaches. So there's all different layers to the massaging of that board up down as you get more information and as the clarity starts to build. >> And by the time you turn the card in and I get here, you probably feel like you know the young man pretty well. >> Oh yeah, there's no doubt about it. I mean, you know, there's you've gone over him so shoot, we just walked out of the the meeting right now and you've gone over these guys so much and but that's that's why you do it. It's there there always comes a moment of clarity and that's what I think is the best part of our job or the most gratifying is is it could be in fall visit you might have that clarity of this is the guy he's not moving from the board at this point and and it stays that way all the way through or there's guys that it takes a little bit of time you got to get the all-star games you got to get the combine you got to get a coach's vision but at some point or you're at the proday live and you're looking at the guy move around and you find the clarity some point that clarity comes and that's what we're searching for and by draft night we'll have clarity on every one of those guys. >> That's why draft season is 365 days a year as I always say on my podcast. So you talk about collaboration with the scouting staff. I I one of my favorite kind of uh threads to weave is is the collaboration between you guys and the coaching staff because you know sometimes coaches maybe want more of a football player. Sometimes maybe the scouting staff wants to trace, right? You have to find a way to marry that together. Just talk about the ideal collaboration between scouting staff and coaching staff if you can. I I think that's extremely important, you know, because there comes a certain point in the draft or in free agency depending on the money that you're paying a player. Uh there's a layer in the draft whether that could be second round one year, it could be fourth round and below the next year, you know, it just varies uh based on the year, but there comes a point where there aren't the players that are they can do it all. They might be really good at one thing and not so good at the other and need development in another aspect. Well, we need the coaches to help us find that vision of how they're going to use this player and and what can we develop because there are everyone's flawed. We're all flawed and so are the players. So, we got to know the vision from the coaches. Are they going to be put into certain positions to, you know, extenduate their their strengths and not their weaknesses. So, the vision of how the players going to be used um is extremely important. >> It's more like we're not drafting a guy for Huya today, but who's going to be >> Yes. you're always always thinking about year one, but but we're never, you know, discounting down the road and what he's going to be, you know, at the end of his contract. >> Yeah, it makes perfect sense. So, we talked a lot about uh John Eric Sullivan and your relationship, but how about some other mentors you've come across in your time in the NFL that have really had a profound impact on you in this job? >> Yeah, I've been fortunate to, you know, I've been around some really, you know, elite football people uh throughout my career. My my dad obviously AJ Smith was a general manager for 10 years in the Chargers, alltime winning as GM in Charger history. So I I was born and raised in the personnel side. John Eric was born and raised in the in the coaching side obviously with his dad being an elite coach. Um but even so a lot of my what I believe in the pillars, your foundations come from him. Um he was with the Buffalo Bills and learned under Bill Poland the Hall of Famer. Um, and then when I got to the league, I started in Washington. Mike Shanahan, Kyle, you know, the tree that that's talked about all the time. Kyle Shanahan floor, all those guys. Um, they were on the coaching side. I was on the personnel side. But to learn under and watch Mike Shanahan, coach, you know, was was unbelievable. And still some of the things that he would say, you you you carry on as you as you go through the process. Um, but I would I've been fortunate to be around a lot of really talented football minds. I get the sense that maybe in first grade when your teacher asked you to write what you want to be when you grow up, you might have said something about being in football. >> Yes. Yeah. No, I thought I was going to be a player for a long time and then when I found out I wasn't good enough, you know, then it was definitely, you know, following my dad's footsteps. >> What's the What's your favorite part of a job? >> I, you know, there there's so much like this time of year like February meetings and on is really that's probably my favorite part of the job. it. The favorite like moments are what we were just talking about earlier, that clarity when when you find that clarity of, okay, this guy's going here on the board and he's staying there and that's where it is and you're hoping that it falls a certain way. But it's the it's finding that clarity because it's not it's not hard. It's or it's not easy, I should say. You know, there there's times that you need the full process to go through guys and you're trying to figure them out. Um, but you always come up with that moment of clarity and and that's what I that's what I love about it. the satisfaction of the culmination of all the work kind of crystallizing there. No doubt. >> Let's conclude with this. We have seven picks in the top 100 this year, 11 overall. I can't wait for it. Personally, I'm sure you guys feel the same way. What are you most excited about for this year's draft? >> I mean, just just adding. I mean, it's, you know, it's we're going to get good football players at every level. It's not just the, you know, the number. Obviously, the number more picks you have, the more shots you have on target and on goal, as they say, more chances you have to hit. But um you know that doesn't necessarily mean that we're going to have 11. We got 11 going in, we might have less. Maybe we trade up and and do all those things or we gather more for for next year. So there's a lot of different you got a lot of flexibility when you have that kind of capital. But um there's definitely uh we're excited about the draft. We're excited about the volume um and how we can impact the team not only this year but as we talked about earlier moving forward. >> A lot that can happen for your Miami Dolphins come draft weekend. He's assistant general manager Kyle Smith. Kyle, we appreciate your time today, man. Thank you. >> Thanks. Thanks, man.
